payload.title: Shared log: ledger audit omits claim conflicts; conflict detection can be spurious
payload.body: FEAT-694 review. (1) LedgerService._shared_log_audit (ledger/service.py) does not report claim conflicts; they exist only in the transient SharedLogImportReport and are lost when hooks redirect output to /dev/null (AC10 partly met). (2) import_shared_log's claim-conflict loop compares imported issue.claimed payloads with the final claimed_by, so history 'A claims, A unclaims, B claims' yields a bogus A-vs-B conflict. Fix: flag only claims that lost / ignore claims superseded by later unclaimed/closed; persist or recompute conflicts statelessly for audit; add an audit test.

payload.body: FEAT-694 review suggestions, all in ledger/shared_log.py unless noted: rotate_events appends to archives before os.replace of current, so a crash duplicates lines (skip event_ids already in archive); rotation moves every non-issue.* event, spec says only task.*/spec.*/insight.*; export_events appends without ensuring existing file ends in newline; digest_files/_stable_relative_path key off first 'sdd' path component (use relative_to(repo_root)); LedgerService.claim pre-import checks only events.jsonl existence, should use shared_log_files(); cli.py --stage subprocess check=True CalledProcessError uncaught; spec §1 lacks explicit 'superseded by FEAT-694' marker for the FEAT-671 non-goal (AC13).

payload.title: test_report CLI can exit non-zero / skip output, contradicting "never blocks" in /sdd-done §4.7
payload.body: scripts/sdd/test_report.py main() returns 2 on an unreadable index or bad args and prints nothing; args.out.write_text is unguarded (OSError -> exit 1). With an empty DECISION and no $TEST_REPORT_MD, `gh pr create --body-file "$TEST_REPORT_MD"` in the hotfix/fallback commands fails on a missing file. Fix: on an unusable index emit a minimal "## Tests — no data" section and return 0; catch OSError on --out; guard --body-file in the .md text.

jira_cli auth accepts a bare pasted code without any state/CSRF check
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/jira_cli.py (auth command, ~lines 288-292): a pasted full redirect URL is state-checked with hmac.compare_digest, but a bare code only logs a warning and proceeds, so a stripped-down paste bypasses the CSRF check. Spec AC3 says a state mismatch aborts. Suggested fix: require the full redirect URL, or gate bare codes behind an explicit --allow-bare-code flag. Found by the FEAT-696 independent review.

payload.title: sdd-coder blast-radius collector always exits 1 in worktrees (no wiki plane) — contract-symbol tasks forced to strong seats
payload.body: _collect_wiki_blast (complexity_collectors.py:643-666) runs `python -m parrot.knowledge.wiki.cli symbols blast --path <worktree> ...` with cwd=worktree. A feature worktree has no `.parrot/wiki` plane (it lives only in the main checkout), so the CLI exits 1 with "Wiki not built yet for <path>. Run `wikitoolkit build` first." — reproduced 2026-10-17 by running the exact command against a path without a wiki plane. The collector records `blast_symbols` state=unknown ("Blast radius incomplete (sym:...: exit 1)"), and ComplexityPolicy routes `unknown` like `complex` (strong_models allowlist only, commit 957c15d96). Net effect measured in artifacts/logs/sdd-coder-usage: October 2026 has 93 unknown + 186 complex vs 26 standard assessments — ~91% of tasks bypass the cheap seats (nova glm/minimax/qwen/mistral, gemini, codex-spark, haiku) and land on gpt-5.6-terra / native sonnet. Every task that declares Codebase Contract symbols is systematically classified unknown. Fix direction: resolve the wiki plane from the main checkout (git rev-parse --git-common-dir parent, same pattern as telemetry.resolve_durable_root) instead of the worktree path, or fall back to the main-checkout plane when the worktree has none; symbols genuinely missing from the plane should still yield missing-root unknown, but plane-absent must not.

payload.title: parrot e2e up: detached daemon stops gracefully when the launcher exits normally (AC5 survival not met)
payload.body: Found by the real-subprocess scenario test_up_daemon_and_target_survive_launcher_exit (packages/ai-parrot-server/tests/e2e/test_up_detached_lifecycle.py, brief issue:792b6e2a8f25). `python -m parrot.e2e.cli up mcp-stdio` exits 0 with a ready RunState, but immediately afterwards the daemon (supervisor_identity) is gone and the persisted state is status=stopped, cleanup_complete=true, shutdown_forced=false, with no `down` call: a graceful stop (SIGTERM/SIGINT path in cli.py _run_daemon). The target dies right after the daemon. Reproduced manually 3x inside the Bash sandbox and under pytest. By contrast, SIGKILLing the launcher mid-wait leaves daemon+target alive (scenario 2 passes), so the trigger is specific to the launcher's normal exit. Cause not identified; candidates: a signal sent at launcher interpreter/asyncio teardown, or a sandbox pid-namespace artifact (unverified outside the sandbox). Suggested: re-run the scenario outside bwrap; if it still fails, trace which signal reaches the daemon (cli.py:_run_daemon signal handlers at ~653) and fix _spawn_detached_target (cli.py:467). Then drop the xfail marker on the scenario.

payload.title: FormDesigner Teams submit: tenant isolation silently depends on formdesigner_submit_secret
payload.body: verify_envelope() checks https, host allowlist and that the path matches {api_base_path}/{tenant}/forms/{form_uid}/data, but the envelope's tenant/form_uid are client-supplied card data. The HMAC check only runs when formdesigner_submit_secret is set. With the secret unset, a Teams user can craft an Action.Submit payload targeting another tenant/form on an allowed host, and the bot forwards it with its own formdesigner_submit_token bearer. Undocumented. Fix options: document that the secret is required when a bearer token is configured, log a startup warning (or refuse bearer use) when token is set without secret, and cover it in the MSTeams FormDesigner docs.

payload.title: AC-5 wording conflicts with the spec's own deterministic-sort requirement
payload.body: sdd/specs/dev-loop-pool-exclusive-tasks.spec.md AC-5 says run_wave call arguments, pool size and should_fan_out results must be 'identical to the pre-change behaviour' for a legacy index. But partition_wave() (task_scheduler.py:84) unconditionally sorts every wave by TaskRef.id, per an explicit Pattern to Follow in spec section 7 ('Sort by TaskRef.id explicitly: next_wave() returns tasks in no particular order'). Since the pre-change code passed scheduler.next_wave() (a Python Set, non-deterministic iteration order) straight to run_wave, and DevAgentPool.run_wave (agent_pool.py:476) assigns workers positionally by list index, a legacy multi-task wave's worker/backend/model assignment can differ from pre-change runs under the new deterministic sort. This is a net improvement (deterministic vs hash-order-dependent) and was independently confirmed correct/intentional by code review (codex + code-reviewer subagent) against FEAT-560's own architecture section, but AC-5's literal wording should be reconciled with section 7's explicit sort requirement so future readers don't file this as a regression. Suggested fix: amend AC-5 to scope 'identical' to the set of dispatched tasks and pool sizing, not raw list order, or add a note that TaskRef.id-sorted worker assignment is an intentional, accepted behavior change.

payload.title: Misleading comment implies merge/refresh only runs on exclusive rounds
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/flows/dev_loop/nodes/development.py, the comment above the isolated-mode merge_sequential/refresh_all call in _execute_pool's round loop reads '# For exclusive rounds, merge and refresh before the next batch'. The block it labels is gated only on 'manager is not None' (isolated mode), not on is_exclusive, so it correctly runs after EVERY round per AC-6 -- the comment just describes the wrong condition and could mislead a future maintainer into thinking the merge/refresh is exclusive-round-specific. payload.title: engine.py reaches into ExecutionPool private state from multiple methods instead of its public API
payload.body: engine.py repeatedly does 'from parrot.flows.dev_loop.sdd_coder.pool import _effective_key' (4 separate local imports across begin_execution/suspend_model/_select_retry_seat/_classify_and_suspend) and reaches into pool._admitted, pool._condition, pool._seats, pool._busy_seats, pool._seat_views, pool._status, pool._cached_assigner, pool._local_exclusions, pool._generation from multiple methods. pool.py's own docstrings emphasize a clean admit/release/suspend/view/assigner API and 'never shares mutable state'. This encapsulation erosion directly enabled a confirmed CRITICAL bug (fixed in commit 84ede6b60): _classify_and_suspend's retry-path call passed a str (attempts[-1].seat_label) where a RosterSeat was required, silently swallowed by run_chunk's return_exceptions=True gather. Recommend adding a couple of narrow accessor methods on ExecutionPool (e.g. resolve_admission(attempt_uid) -> tuple[str, ModelKey], current_status() -> ExecutionStatus) so engine.py stops reaching into pool internals directly, with type checking able to catch this class of bug at the boundary.

payload.title: end_execution's snapshot-enrichment loop constructs an invalid AttemptRecord as a dict.get default
payload.body: engine.py's end_execution() snapshot-enrichment loop (introduced by TASK-3282) has: manager_key = f"{task_id}.a{self._latest_attempt.get(task_id, AttemptRecord(attempt=1)).attempt}". Python evaluates dict.get's default argument EAGERLY regardless of whether the key is present, and AttemptRecord requires seat_label/started_at with no defaults -- so this line raises pydantic ValidationError whenever the loop body executes for a task_id not already in self._latest_attempt, which is ALWAYS true for a native task (native tasks never populate _latest_attempt; that bookkeeping only happens in _run_task, which native dispatch bypasses entirely per design). Reproduced directly during this feature's final code review by transiently exposing this loop via a status-transition change (since reverted); the SAME commit (84ede6b60) also widened end_execution's busy-check gate from 'view.status == active' to 'view.status != closed', which now makes the busy-check raise execution_busy BEFORE this loop can ever run in practice as long as native_reservations/admitted_attempts is non-empty -- but the underlying construction is still broken and would crash if ever reached (e.g. a future code path that reaches this loop with an empty pool.snapshot() but a still-populated self._native_reservations). Fix: replace the eager default with a lazy lookup, e.g.  and skip/attempt=1 literal when existing is None, never constructing an under-specified AttemptRecord.

payload.title: test_execution_pool_integration.py uses blocking subprocess.run inside async def tests (ASYNC221/240)
payload.body: New file test_execution_pool_integration.py (TASK-3282/3285) builds throwaway git sandboxes with subprocess.run(...) directly inside async def test functions, never off the event loop -- a direct violation of codebase-conventions.md's 'never block the event loop'. ruff check on this file reports 40 ASYNC221 findings (all subprocess.run-inside-async-def call sites). payload.title: MSTeams wrapper aiohttp sessions never closed on IntegrationManager.shutdown()
payload.body: IntegrationManager.shutdown() (packages/ai-parrot-integrations/src/parrot/integrations/manager.py) only calls self.msteams_bots.clear(); it never awaits wrapper.close_formdesigner_client() (FEAT-551) nor the pre-existing close_voice_transcriber(). payload.title: FormDesigner Teams submit: tenant isolation silently depends on formdesigner_submit_secret
payload.body: verify_envelope() checks https, host allowlist and that the path matches {api_base_path}/{tenant}/forms/{form_uid}/data, but the envelope's tenant/form_uid are client-supplied card data. The HMAC check only runs when formdesigner_submit_secret is set. With the secret unset, a Teams user can craft an Action.Submit payload targeting another tenant/form on an allowed host, and the bot forwards it with its own formdesigner_submit_token bearer. Undocumented. Fix options: document that the secret is required when a bearer token is configured, log a startup warning (or refuse bearer use) when token is set without secret, and cover it in the MSTeams FormDesigner docs.

Only the 403 half exists (packages/ai-parrot-integrations/tests/msteams/test_formdesigner_roundtrip.py::test_teams_card_private_form_403). The bearer -> 200 path is not exercised end-to-end. payload.title: AC-5 wording conflicts with the spec's own deterministic-sort requirement
payload.body: sdd/specs/dev-loop-pool-exclusive-tasks.spec.md AC-5 says run_wave call arguments, pool size and should_fan_out results must be 'identical to the pre-change behaviour' for a legacy index. But partition_wave() (task_scheduler.py:84) unconditionally sorts every wave by TaskRef.id, per an explicit Pattern to Follow in spec section 7 ('Sort by TaskRef.id explicitly: next_wave() returns tasks in no particular order'). Since the pre-change code passed scheduler.next_wave() (a Python Set, non-deterministic iteration order) straight to run_wave, and DevAgentPool.run_wave (agent_pool.py:476) assigns workers positionally by list index, a legacy multi-task wave's worker/backend/model assignment can differ from pre-change runs under the new deterministic sort. This is a net improvement (deterministic vs hash-order-dependent) and was independently confirmed correct/intentional by code review (codex + code-reviewer subagent) against FEAT-560's own architecture section, but AC-5's literal wording should be reconciled with section 7's explicit sort requirement so future readers don't file this as a regression. Suggested fix: amend AC-5 to scope 'identical' to the set of dispatched tasks and pool sizing, not raw list order, or add a note that TaskRef.id-sorted worker assignment is an intentional, accepted behavior change.

payload.title: sdd-coder: complex/unknown tasks get zero retries — the retry ladder is MCP-only, so a native strong seat serves attempt 1 but is invisible to attempt 2
payload.body:
## Symptom

A complex/unknown task that fails attempt 1 on an MCP strong seat is blocked with
`complex_model_unavailable: no eligible retry seat for <TASK-ID>` and never retries, even with a
strong seat idle. Seen on TASK-3565 (FEAT-584): `dirty_task_worktree` on attempt 1, then blocked.
The orchestrator blamed the native `sonnet` seat being busy on a sibling task. That is wrong.

## Mechanism

`eligible_seats()` (roster.py:240-281) restricts complex/unknown to `complexity.strong_models`.
Both retry selectors then unconditionally skip native seats:

- `SddCoderEngine._select_retry_seat` — engine.py:2459-2464 (`if seat.kind == "native": continue`)
- `ChunkAssigner.retry_seat` — roster.py:411

The guard itself is right: a native seat has no dispatcher (it is an `Agent` call `sdd-worker` makes
via `coder_prepare_native`), so returning one hits `_run_attempt`'s `assert seat.backend is not None`
instead of retrying — the TASK-3554 crash fix.

The defect is the resulting asymmetry: a native strong seat is dispatch-capable for attempt 1 but
invisible to attempt 2. With strong seats = {gpt-5.6-terra (mcp), sonnet (native)}, the retry set for
a task started on terra is `{terra, sonnet} - tried{terra} - native{sonnet} = {}` — structurally
empty on every first-attempt failure.

## The "seat was busy" reading is wrong

`_select_retry_seat` returns `None` immediately here. Its `has_busy_healthy` wait loop
(engine.py:2489-2500) applies the same two filters (skip native, skip `tried_seats`), so no candidate
reaches the busy check and it never waits. The block reproduces with every other seat idle. The
current diagnostic text sends operators hunting a scheduling race that does not exist.

## Evidence

- `.claude/worktrees/feat-FEAT-584-sdd-execution-optimization--pool/TASK-3565-a1-d4a1d075d068474fa254201190e68fa8`
  holds 3 modified-but-uncommitted files with HEAD still on the prior task's commit — the
  `dirty_task_worktree` (engine.py:1517) that triggered the retry.
- `eligible_seats()` over the then-current roster: `retry_capable=['gpt-5.6-terra']` for complex and
  unknown alike.

## Mitigation applied (config, not a fix)

`.parrot/mcp-toolkits.yaml` gained a second strong MCP seat (`gpt-5.6-luna`, backend codex), so
`retry_capable` is now `['gpt-5.6-terra', 'gpt-5.6-luna']`. Any roster with one MCP strong seat still
reproduces this — including the shipped default
`packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/mcp/_toolkit_templates/sdd-coder.yaml`.

## Proposed fix

Make the native seat retry-capable: have the retry path yield a `NativePrep`-shaped handoff that
`sdd-worker` runs itself (the same handoff `prepare_native` already does for attempt 1) instead of
routing through `dispatcher.dispatch`.

Smaller independent sub-fixes:

1. When the restricted retry set is non-empty but all-native, say so
   (`only native strong seats remain; the retry ladder is MCP-only`) instead of the generic
   "no eligible retry seat", which reads as transient capacity.
2. At `coder_begin_execution`, warn when `strong_models` resolves to fewer than 2 MCP seats — a
   roster that can never retry a complex task should be reported at start, not on first failure.
3. Fix the shipped template default, which ships exactly the reproducing roster.

payload.title: GoogleCodingDispatcher writes its --json-schema to the host /tmp, which agy --sandbox cannot read — the google_coding seat fails every dispatch
payload.body:
## Symptom

Every `google_coding` (agy) dispatch fails immediately, before the model runs:

```
DispatchExecutionError: agy CLI dispatch failed with exit code 1:
Error: invalid --json-schema: failed to read schema file
"/tmp/dev_loop_agy_schema_so0wy9ca.json": open ...: no such file or directory
```

Fails in ~0.2s with exit code 1. The file *does* exist on the host at that moment — it is unlinked
only in the `finally` at google_coding.py:281-286.

## Root cause

`GoogleCodingDispatcher._materialize_json_schema` (google_coding.py:361-373) uses
`tempfile.mkstemp()`, i.e. the host temp dir. `GoogleCodingDispatchProfile.sandbox` defaults to
`True` (models/google_coding.py:29), and `_build_command` passes `--sandbox` (google_coding.py:311).
`agy --sandbox` runs with a **private /tmp**, so a host temp path is not visible inside it. The
schema path is the only argument pointing outside the workspace.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-09-21, agy 1.2.0)

Run from a worktree under `WORKTREE_BASE_PATH`:

- `agy --json-schema /tmp/probe.json --output-format json --sandbox --print='...'`
  → `failed to read schema file ... no such file or directory`
- `agy --json-schema .probe.json --output-format json --sandbox --print='...'`
  (identical file, inside cwd) → `"status":"SUCCESS"` with a correct `structured_output` object.

Only the schema's location differs.

## Impact

The `google_coding` backend is unusable as an sdd-coder seat today. It is silently masked: the
`RosterProbe` smoke call fails the same way, so the seat is dropped as "unavailable" and looks like a
credentials/CLI problem rather than a dispatcher bug. `sdd/state/FEAT-549/design_research/open_questions.txt`
records the agy fallback validation as never executed, which is why this survived.

## Proposed fix

Materialize the schema **inside `cwd`** rather than the host temp dir, and keep the existing `finally`
unlink.

Care is needed on placement: an untracked leftover in the worktree root would make
`SddCoderEngine._consolidate` (engine.py:1517, `git status --porcelain -uall`) report
`dirty_task_worktree` and fail an otherwise-good attempt if the process is killed before cleanup.
Write it somewhere `git status` does not see — e.g. under the worktree's git dir, or a path already
ignored — rather than a bare dotfile in the worktree root.

Add a regression test asserting the schema path passed to `--json-schema` is under `cwd`
(packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/test_google_coding_dispatcher.py).

## Related

Discovered while validating `gemini-3.8-flash-high` as a second strong MCP seat for
[[issue:569e81756247]] (complex tasks get zero retries). That seat had to fall back to
codex/`gpt-5.6-luna` because of this bug. Note also that agy model ids are effort-suffixed
(`gemini-3.8-flash-high`); a bare `gemini-3.8-flash` is not a valid id, and
`parrot/flows/dev_loop/catalog.py`'s `google_coding` models tuple lists bare, stale names
(`gemini-3.6-flash`, `gemini-3.0-pro`).

payload.title: test_voice_in_voice_out_flow fails: patch() cannot resolve lazily-exported telegram.wrapper submodule
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-integrations/tests/voice/tts/test_tts_integration.py::test_voice_in_voice_out_flow fails with 'AttributeError: module parrot.integrations.telegram has no attribute wrapper' when run standalone (PYTHONPATH=packages/ai-parrot-integrations/src only, matching a fresh worktree checkout). The test does 'with patch("parrot.integrations.telegram.wrapper.CallbackRegistry")'; unittest.mock on Python 3.12 resolves this via pkgutil.resolve_name, which backs off to getattr(parrot.integrations.telegram, "wrapper") when importing the full dotted path fails on the first attempt inside a pytest session, and __init__.py's lazy __getattr__ (_LAZY_EXPORTS, line 56) does not list "wrapper", so it raises instead of falling through to a real import. Confirmed pre-existing: reproduced identically at commit f5c2350b0 (FEAT-591's base commit, before any FEAT-591 task ran) via a throwaway git worktree, so it is unrelated to FEAT-591's TASK-3619/TASK-3621 diffs. A plain 'python -c "import parrot.integrations.telegram.wrapper"' succeeds fine; only the mock.patch dotted-path resolution path fails, suggesting a namespace-package / sys.modules interaction specific to pytest's import mode. Suggested fix: add "wrapper" (and other real submodules under parrot.integrations.telegram) to _LAZY_EXPORTS as self-referential entries, or change the test to patch via 'from parrot.integrations.telegram import wrapper as wrapper_mod; patch.object(wrapper_mod, "CallbackRegistry")'.

payload.title: Review TASK-3642
DetectionBox.class_id/class_name/area are non-Optional but default to None, breaking JSON round-trips
payload.body: DetectionBox (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/models/detections.py:37-56) declares class_id: int, class_name: str, area: int with default=None but WITHOUT Optional[...] typing. A plain model_dump_json() on any DetectionBox (or a model containing one, e.g. PerceptionResult) writes an explicit null for these three fields when they were never set. Reloading that JSON via model_validate_json() then fails Pydantic v2 validation ('Input should be a valid integer', 'Input should be a valid string') because an EXPLICIT null on a non-Optional field is validated, unlike an omitted key which falls back to the (unvalidated) default. Discovered via FEAT-592 TASK-3643's test_nova2_cli.py, which builds --boxes override fixtures by round-tripping a PerceptionResult through model_dump_json()/model_validate_json(); worked around there with exclude_none=True (commit 850539844) since packages/ is out of scope for FEAT-592 (G3/AC6). Suggested fix: type the three fields Optional[int]/Optional[str]/Optional[int] (matching their None defaults), matching the existing Optional[str] pattern already used for label/ocr_text two lines below in the same class.

payload.title: Review TASK-3643
review_checkpoint prepare always fails checkpoint_busy after any coder_run_chunk dispatch
payload.body: CoderEngine._job_worktrees (engine.py:383) records job_id -> worktree at dispatch time (line 3588) and is NEVER pruned anywhere in the file (verified: only 2 write sites, both additive; grep for del/pop finds none). end_execution's snapshot enrichment (engine.py:859-861) unconditionally copies EVERY job_id in _job_worktrees matching the closing worktree into snapshot.outstanding_job_ids, with no check of the job's actual terminal state. review_checkpoint.prepare_review_checkpoint (checkpoint.py:483-489) then treats any non-empty outstanding_job_ids as CheckpointBusyError, unconditionally. Net effect: once a worktree has dispatched at least one coder_run_chunk job in the engine process's lifetime, coder_end_execution's own published settlement snapshot can NEVER have an empty outstanding_job_ids, so 'python -m scripts.sdd.review_checkpoint prepare' permanently fails with checkpoint_busy for that worktree, even when every job is independently confirmed state=done/outcome=completed via coder_wait/coder_status (reproduced on FEAT-592: 4 jobs, all coder_status-verified done, coder_end_execution returned status=closed, yet review_checkpoint prepare reported '4 job(s)' outstanding). Suggested fix: only append a job_id to outstanding_job_ids when its recorded state is not a terminal one (running/unknown), or remove/mark job_ids from _job_worktrees once coder_wait/coder_status observes a terminal state.

Every other I/O operation in nova2.py is correctly routed through CpuExecutor.run/asyncio.to_thread (e.g. cv2.imread, the detections.json/run.json writes); these two are the only inconsistency, a literal (if low-impact, small-JSON-at-startup) violation of CLAUDE.md's 'no blocking I/O in async contexts'. payload.title: Review TASK-3623
coder_end_execution never clears _job_worktrees, permanently blocking review_checkpoint prepare
payload.body: SddCoderEngine._job_worktrees (engine.py:383) is set once per dispatched coder_run_chunk job (engine.py:3588, self._job_worktrees[job.job_id] = ctx.worktree) and is never deleted anywhere in the module (grep confirms only 4 references: init, set, and two read-only enumerations). coder_end_execution's snapshot enrichment (engine.py:859-862) unconditionally appends every job_id in _job_worktrees whose worktree matches the closing execution's worktree_path into the durable ExecutionSnapshot.outstanding_job_ids, regardless of whether coder_status/coder_wait already reported that job's state as 'done'. The gate at engine.py:839 that is supposed to refuse close on outstanding jobs reads pool.snapshot() BEFORE this enrichment (pool.py:207/219 shows native_reservations/outstanding_job_ids are intentionally empty at that layer), so the gate is a no-op and end_execution always reports status='closed' even with stale job ids present. scripts/sdd/review_checkpoint.py's prepare_review_checkpoint (checkpoint.py:472-489) then reads that persisted, polluted snapshot and correctly refuses with checkpoint_busy ('N job(s)') for every execution that ever ran coder_run_chunk at least once -- observed live on FEAT-591 execution a3f1c2e4-7b6d-4a89-9e0f-2c8d5b4a1f37: job-2ecb8c316215 (coder_run_chunk for TASK-3623) completed cleanly per coder_status (state=done, all tasks merged) at 13:16:00Z, coder_end_execution succeeded ~13:26Z, yet review_checkpoint prepare still reports '0 attempt(s), 0 reservation(s), 1 job(s)' outstanding, permanently blocking the FEAT-584 M8 review-checkpoint step described in the sdd-worker Completion protocol for any feature whose worker used the MCP dispatch path at all. Suggested fix: pop the job_id from self._job_worktrees once its terminal state is durably observed (e.g. in status()/wait() when job.state == 'done', or filter outstanding_job_ids in the enrichment loop to jobs whose self._jobs[job_id].state != 'done').

payload.title: BasicAgent.speech_tts_options is a shared class-level mutable dict default
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/agent.py:75 declares 'speech_tts_options: Dict[str, Any] = {}' at class scope on plain (non-Pydantic) BasicAgent, with no per-instance copy in __init__. This single dict object is shared by every BasicAgent instance process-wide, mirroring the pre-existing 'speakers' anti-pattern one line below. Currently safe because the only read site (agent.py ~686, 'config_values = dict(self.speech_tts_options)') copies before use, so there is no live bug. Any future in-place mutation (e.g. agent.speech_tts_options['polly_engine'] = 'x') would silently leak across every agent instance. Fix: copy the default in __init__ (self.speech_tts_options = dict(speech_tts_options or {})). Found during FEAT-591 adversarial code review; deferred as non-blocking (not yet exploitable).

payload.title: speech_report narrator selection raises unhandled StopIteration on empty self.speakers
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/bots/agent.py ~735: 'speaker_data = dict(next(iter(self.speakers.values())))' picks the narrator for non-Gemini script mode. If a subclass ever sets self.speakers = {}, this raises an unhandled StopIteration instead of a clear error. Low risk today (class default always has 2 entries) but worth a guard with a clearer error message. Found during FEAT-591 adversarial code review; deferred as non-blocking.

Harmless, but outside FEAT-591's stated task scope and the repo's 'minimal, focused diffs' rule -- likely an artifact of an engine lint-autofix commit. payload.title: No speech_report-level test for google_tts + verbatim zero-LLM-calls path
payload.body: Only supertonic and aws_polly have an agent-level test asserting 'zero LLM calls' in verbatim mode via speech_report itself (test_speech_report_verbatim_supertonic_zero_llm_calls, plus the Polly extension test). google_tts is fully covered at the backend unit level (test_google_backend.py) but not exercised through speech_report(). Minor coverage gap -- the routing code is backend-agnostic so risk is low. Found during FEAT-591 adversarial code review.

payload.title: Doc phrasing inconsistency: '3000 chars per chunk' vs actual 2800-char boundary
payload.body: docs/voice/speech-report-tts-backends.md:189 says long-form 'supports longer text (up to 3000 chars per chunk)' while the implementation's actual chunk boundary is 2800 chars (_MAX_CHARS = 2800 in polly_backend.py:15, matching AC8 and correctly documented two sections later at line 200). Slightly inconsistent phrasing (3000 is Polly's hard synthesize_speech limit, not the chunk size), not functionally wrong. Found during FEAT-591 adversarial code review.

payload.reason: Copied speech_tts_options in BasicAgent.__init__ so the class-level dict default is never shared/mutated across instances.

payload.title: FEAT-592: --region-prefix has no CLI flag, silently breaks non-us Bedrock regions
payload.body: examples/planogram/aws/nova2.py hardcodes DEFAULT_REGION_PREFIX = "us" and always passes it to NovaVisionClient.create(region_prefix=...); --region only sets the AWS endpoint region, never the geo inference-profile prefix, and there is no --region-prefix flag even though NovaVisionClient.create (nova_vision.py) accepts one. README.md's own 'Known limitations' #4 explicitly claims other regions 'need the matching prefix (eu., jp., global.)' but the CLI provides no way to set it, so a --region eu-west-1 run would still resolve us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 and almost certainly fail. Confirmed independently by two reviewers (code-reviewer + sdd-secondopinion) during FEAT-592's post-merge adversarial review. Suggested fix: add a --region-prefix flag (default 'us') to nova2.py's argparse, thread it into NovaVisionClient.create, and keep the README's multi-region claim honest.

payload.title: FEAT-592: nova2.py's async main() calls blocking file I/O synchronously
payload.body: examples/planogram/aws/nova2.py's async def main() calls load_perception(args.boxes, image) and load_planogram_vocabulary(args.planogram) directly — plain Path.read_text()/json.loads(), not routed through CpuExecutor.run/asyncio.to_thread the way the same function's detections.json/run.json writes are. Inconsistent with the project's async-first rule (CLAUDE.md) and the feature's own spec text: 'Every OpenCV and file-I/O operation goes through CpuExecutor.run.' Low practical impact for this single-run CLI (small local JSON files) but a genuine, spec-named convention deviation. Confirmed by two independent reviewers during FEAT-592's post-merge review. Suggested fix: wrap both calls in executor.run(...) or asyncio.to_thread(...) like the JSON writes already are.

payload.title: FEAT-592: NovaVisionClient reaches into NovaClient's underscore-prefixed internals
payload.body: examples/planogram/aws/nova_vision.py's NovaVisionClient.create()/.resolved_region call nova._translate_model(...) and read nova._region — underscore-prefixed BedrockConverseBase/NovaClient internals (verified real, not hallucinated: bedrock.py:424, bedrock.py:313). The feature's spec explicitly sanctions this reach-through as a prototype for eventual first-class BedrockConverseBase image support, but it is fragile coupling that could silently break on an unrelated client refactor. Confirmed by two independent reviewers during FEAT-592's post-merge review. No action required unless/until BedrockConverseBase grows first-class image support, at which point this shim should be retired in favor of the real API.

payload.title: FEAT-592: unused Any/Tuple imports in nova2.py
payload.body: examples/planogram/aws/nova2.py imports Any and Tuple from typing but never references either in the file body (verified by grep). Does not fail ruff check because ruff.toml's per-file-ignores exempts examples/**/*.py from F401, so this is dead code only, not a CI-blocking issue. Confirmed by two independent reviewers during FEAT-592's post-merge review. Trivial cleanup: drop the two unused names from the import line.

payload.title: test_all_seats_exhausted fails on dev: isolated_suspension_store is not isolated (resolves to the shared .parrot/ledger)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/tests/flows/dev_loop/sdd_coder/test_engine_plan_merge.py::test_all_seats_exhausted fails on origin/dev (a89d61aa5, verified in the main checkout independently of FEAT-599): 'assert view.fallback_required is True' -> False. The conftest fixture isolated_suspension_store builds CoderSuspensionStore.from_root(tmp_path), which goes through LedgerService.from_root -> find_shared_root(root) and opens the SHARED <shared-root>/.parrot/ledger/ledger.db rather than a ledger under tmp_path. Observed during FEAT-599 validation: the pool view rendered in the failing assertion carried a suspension record for TASK-0003 / execution 908fd577-... that the test never wrote, i.e. records from other test runs (and from real sdd-coder runs) leak into recent(), and conversely the engine tests under sdd_coder/ append synthetic suspensions (native/haiku timeouts, 30-min cooldown) into the developer's real ledger on every run. Suggested fix: make the fixture point CoderSuspensionStore at a LedgerLog rooted strictly under tmp_path (or monkeypatch find_shared_root), and assert in the test that recent() is empty before seeding.

payload.title: Stale installer action-count assertions after bookstore MCP default landed
payload.body: `install_claude_integration()` (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/claude_code/installer.py:969) defaults `bookstore: bool = True`, which appends 2 actions ("bookstore MCP — installed", ".claude/skills/bookstore/SKILL.md — installed") to every fresh install. `tests/knowledge/wiki/test_claude_code.py::TestInstaller::test_fresh_install_writes_all_artifacts` still asserts `len(actions) == 10` and `tests/knowledge/wiki/test_codex_integration.py::test_install_writes_mcp_skill_instructions_and_permissions` asserts `len(actions) == 7` — both stale by the 1-2 bookstore actions the codex variant doesn't add (codex installer likely doesn't call bookstore install, still off by one from a different cause — worth re-checking during the fix). Verified byte-identical on origin/dev (commit ab9f97a82) before FEAT-600 touched anything in these files — pre-existing, not caused by FEAT-600. Fix: update the two hardcoded counts (or assert on content rather than length) to account for the bookstore actions.

payload.title: Review TASK-3696
schema sync crashes for postgres/bigquery: duplicate database_type kwarg in toolkit_for()
payload.body:
producers/live.py:34-41 `toolkit_for()` always passes `database_type=cfg.dialect` when constructing the dialect toolkit. `PostgresToolkit.__init__` (toolkits/postgres.py:98-108) and `BigQueryToolkit.__init__` (toolkits/bigquery.py:42-49) both already hardcode `database_type="postgresql"`/`"bigquery"` in their own `super().__init__(...)` call and accept `**kwargs` (they do NOT declare `database_type` as a named param), so the caller's `database_type=cfg.dialect` kwarg flows through `**kwargs` and collides with the hardcoded one, raising `TypeError: __init__() got multiple values for keyword argument 'database_type'`.

Impact: `wikitoolkit schema sync <origin>` crashes for any postgres or bigquery source — the two primary supported dialects, and the exact scenario used in the spec's own AC1 worked example (`--dialect bigquery`). Only the `SQLToolkit` fallback path (e.g. sqlite) works. This breaks AC2 (sync creates pages) and AC1's worked example for the two dialects that matter most in production.

Confirmed by: `packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_live_producer.py::test_toolkit_choice[postgres-PostgresToolkit]` and `[bigquery-BigQueryToolkit]` both fail with this exact TypeError; verified independently by reading toolkits/postgres.py:98-108 and toolkits/bigquery.py:42-49.

Suggested fix: `toolkit_for()` should only pass `database_type=cfg.dialect` to the generic `SQLToolkit` fallback branch, not to dialect-specific subclasses that already set it internally (e.g. omit the kwarg when `toolkit_class is not SQLToolkit`).

payload.title: Post-merge hook's `schema ingest-ddl --changed --quiet` always fails (missing required --origin/--dialect)
payload.body:
claude_code/assets.py:193 (git_hook_block) adds `{wt_bin} schema ingest-ddl --changed --quiet >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` inside the `if [ ! -f .git ]` guard — placement is correct per AC10, but the command itself always fails. `schema_ingest_ddl` in cli.py declares `--origin` and `--dialect` as `required=True` click options (cli.py:3193-3194) with no fallback that loops over `schema.sources` in config when omitted. Running the exact hook invocation through Click's CliRunner immediately fails at argument parsing with `Error: Missing option '--origin'.` (SystemExit 2).

Because the hook wraps the call in `|| true`, the hook script itself never breaks, but the automated DDL-drift capture on every merge (the entire point of wiring this into the git hook) silently never runs — it is a permanent no-op. `test_schema_hook_assets.py::test_ingest_line_inside_guard` only string-checks placement and never exercises the command, so this gap is untested and unnoticed.

Suggested fix: either give `schema ingest-ddl` a mode that loops over all declared `schema.sources` (deriving origin+dialect from config) when `--origin`/`--dialect` are omitted with `--changed`, or have the hook line itself loop over configured origins.

payload.title: docs/wiki/schema-plane.md: add-source examples show a nonexistent positional DSN argument
payload.body:
docs/wiki/schema-plane.md lines ~45, 48, 79, 90, 292 show `wikitoolkit schema add-source postgres "postgresql://prod.internal/main"` and `wikitoolkit schema add-source postgres ENV:DATABASE_URL` — implying a second positional DSN/connection-string argument. The actual CLI command (cli.py:3146-3152, `schema_add_source`) only declares `@click.argument("alias", required=False)` plus `--dialect` (required) and `--dsn-env` (required, "Environment variable NAME holding the DSN, never the value") — there is no positional DSN argument at all. These doc examples would fail if run (`Got unexpected extra argument`), and they directly contradict the doc's own stated security invariant a few paragraphs later ("The DSN is never stored directly..."). This is a real accuracy defect in AC15's required documentation, not just a formatting nit — a reader following the doc would try to pass a raw connection string on the command line.

Suggested fix: rewrite every `add-source` example to the real form, e.g. `wikitoolkit schema add-source bigquery --dialect bigquery --dsn-env EPSON_BQ_DSN --schemas epson`.

payload.title: docs/wiki/schema-plane.md: wrong cache tier order and wrong DatabaseAgent(schema_plane=...) API example
payload.body:
docs/wiki/schema-plane.md §11 (~line 318-321) states the runtime resolution order as "1. Checks the schema plane first (read-only). 2. Falls back to Redis. 3. Falls back to live introspection" — this is wrong. The actual order implemented in cache.py's `get()` is LRU -> schema_cache -> Redis -> plane -> vector store (plane is tier 2b, AFTER Redis, not first).

The same section's example `DatabaseAgent(schema_plane=SchemaPlaneConfig(root=".parrot", origin="postgres"))` does not match the real API: `agent.py::_resolve_schema_plane` (agent.py:162-177) only special-cases `None`, `str`, and `Path` — a `SchemaPlaneConfig` instance (which per spec §2 doesn't even have `root`/`origin` fields) would be stored as-is and assigned directly to `cache_partition.plane`, breaking at the first `.get_table()`-style call since it isn't a `SchemaPlaneReader`.

Suggested fix: correct the tier-order description to LRU -> schema cache -> Redis -> schema plane -> vector store, and fix the `DatabaseAgent` example to `DatabaseAgent(schema_plane=Path(".parrot/schema"))` (or an already-open `SchemaPlaneService`), matching `_resolve_schema_plane`'s actual accepted types.

payload.title: project.py now transitively pulls the entire parrot.bots agent/LLM framework into every wikitoolkit CLI/git-hook invocation
payload.body:
knowledge/wiki/project.py adds a top-level `from parrot.knowledge.wiki.schema.models import SchemaPlaneConfig` (mirroring the existing `DecisionConfig` pattern). `schema/models.py` imports `parrot.bots.database.models`, and `parrot.bots.__init__` eagerly imports `AbstractBot` -> `clients.base` -> `tools.manager` -> `auth` -> `stores.kb` — i.e. the entire agent/LLM/tool/auth framework now loads at import time for every `wikitoolkit` CLI invocation and every git hook that imports `project.py` (post-commit/post-merge), not just schema-plane commands.

This is not a circular import (no crash) and was explicitly flagged as a watch item in the spec's Codebase Contract (§6, referencing the FEAT-578 circular-import precedent), but the spec's own watch item was about avoiding a cycle, not about avoiding this import-weight regression — a previously lightweight CLI/hook path now has a much heavier, unrelated dependency chain on its startup path. This could materially slow every wiki CLI call and every git hook, not just schema-plane ones.

Suggested fix: import `SchemaPlaneConfig` lazily (function-local) in project.py, or restructure `schema/models.py` to avoid importing `bots.database.models` at module level (e.g. TYPE_CHECKING-only, with the real type resolved at the call site that actually needs `TableMetadata`).

payload.title: SchemaPlaneService.ingest_ddl is not atomic — TOCTOU window can let DDL overwrite a live page
payload.body:
service.py::ingest_ddl (~lines 143-172), for each folded DDL record, does a separate `get_page(...)` read followed by a conditional `upsert_pages`/`add_edges` write — these are not wrapped in a single `_write()` transaction, unlike `SchemaStore.replace_schema_slice`/`_replace_source_slice_conn` which IS atomic (one `_write()` spanning delete+insert). This creates a narrow window where a concurrent `schema sync <origin>` between the read and the write of `ingest_ddl` could let a DDL-derived fact overwrite a page that was just live-synced, violating the spec's core merge-rule guarantee ("a live page is never overwritten by DDL facts", AC5).

Likelihood is low given the CLI's normal sequential invocation model (a human or a single cron job running `sync` and `ingest-ddl` one at a time), but nothing in the code prevents concurrent invocation (e.g. two cron jobs, or a `sync` running while `ingest-ddl --changed` fires from the post-merge hook), and the guarantee is stated as an unconditional acceptance criterion.

Suggested fix: wrap the read-check-write sequence in `ingest_ddl` in the store's own `_write()` async context manager (or an equivalent single-transaction upsert) so the live-page check and any resulting write are atomic, mirroring `replace_schema_slice`.

payload.title: schema sync crashes for postgres/bigquery: toolkit_for() passes duplicate database_type kwarg
payload.body: producers/live.py toolkit_for() always passes database_type=cfg.dialect as an explicit kwarg when instantiating PostgresToolkit/BigQueryToolkit. Both subclasses hardcode their own database_type ("postgresql"/"bigquery") when forwarding to SQLToolkit.__init__ via super().__init__(..., database_type="bigquery", **kwargs), so the caller's kwarg collides with the subclass's own kwarg and construction always raises TypeError: SQLToolkit.__init__() got multiple values for keyword argument 'database_type'. Reproduced live via pytest: packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_live_producer.py::test_toolkit_choice[postgres-PostgresToolkit] and [bigquery-BigQueryToolkit] both FAIL with this exact TypeError. Impact: `wikitoolkit schema sync <origin>` (AC2) is completely non-functional against real Postgres or BigQuery sources — the only two dialects with dedicated toolkit subclasses and the two named in the spec's own AC1 example. Only the SQLToolkit fallback path (generic dialects, exercised via FakeToolkit in other tests) avoids the crash. Suggested fix: in toolkit_for(), either drop database_type from the explicit kwargs when the target class already sets it, or build the kwargs dict and let PostgresToolkit/BigQueryToolkit's own hardcoded value win (pop 'database_type' before calling toolkit_class(**kwargs) for those two subclasses).

payload.title: DDL producer over-counts foreign keys on the reference migration corpus (4 recovered vs documented baseline of 3)
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_ddl_producer.py::test_fold_ddl_task_memory_corpus asserts sum(len(record.metadata.foreign_keys) for record in records) == 3 against tools/working_memory/task_memory/migrations/001_task_memory.sql (this is the exact baseline documented in the spec's own §4 Test Specification: "6 tables, 70 columns, 3 FKs"). Actual run recovers 4 (assert 4 == 3 fails). Likely cause: producers/ddl.py's _fold_create folds both an inline column REFERENCES (_add_inline_fk, called from _add_column) and a separate table-level FOREIGN KEY / ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT (_add_fk) for what may be the same logical relationship, double-counting it when a migration expresses both forms for one column. Impact: AC4's "recovers >= 20 CREATE TABLEs and >= 329 columns" numeric bar is column/table-count based so may still pass, but relation/edge-count fidelity (used for `references` edges and downstream join-path assist in generate_query) is measurably wrong on the one corpus fixture the spec ships as ground truth. Reproduced live via pytest (FAILED, 3 failed overall in this test file's suite run).

payload.title: schema diff falsely reports type divergence due to case-sensitive SQL type-name comparison
payload.body: SchemaPlaneService._metadata_differences (schema/service.py, near line 465) compares live_value = str(live_column.get("type","")) against ddl_value = str(ddl_column.get("type","")) with a plain string equality check — no case normalization. Live introspection typically stores lowercase information_schema type names (e.g. "text"), while the DDL producer's rendered/parsed type strings from sqlglot are typically uppercase (e.g. "TEXT"), so identical columns are reported as divergent. Reproduced live via pytest: packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_ingest_and_diff.py::test_diff_reports_type_mismatch_and_identical_schema FAILS — it expects only {"column:id.type"} (a genuine bigint vs int mismatch) but actually gets {"column:id.type", "column:name.type"} where the extra "name" column has matching text/TEXT types that only differ by case. Impact: AC5 requires "schema diff lists the divergences" — as implemented it also lists spurious non-divergences, undermining the tool's usefulness (every synced table would show phantom drift on nearly every column). Suggested fix: normalize both sides (e.g. .upper() or a shared type-canonicalization helper) before comparing in _metadata_differences.

payload.title: test_sync_then_unchanged_and_lookup is flaky: compares LookupResult equality including a live-computed age_days float
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/test_service.py::test_sync_then_unchanged_and_lookup asserts `await schema_service.lookup("bigquery:epson.sales") == await schema_service.lookup("table:bigquery/epson.sales")`. SchemaPlaneService.lookup() computes age_days = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - introspected_at).total_seconds() / 86400 fresh on every call (service.py, lookup()), so two sequential calls in the same test produce two different age_days floats (observed diff was ~3.8e-7 days, i.e. microseconds), making the equality assertion fail nondeterministically. Reproduced live via pytest — FAILED both times run, with the full diff showing every field identical except age_days. This is the test responsible for exercising AC3 (bigquery:epson.sales and table:bigquery/epson.sales must resolve to the same page) — all non-timestamp fields DID match, so the underlying normalize_ref/lookup behavior appears correct, but AC14 ("all §4 tests pass") is not currently met because this test fails as written. Suggested fix: compare model_dump(exclude={"age_days"}) or freeze/monkeypatch the clock between the two lookup() calls.

payload.title: AC7 (wiki_remember note survives schema sync) and AC4's 32-file/329-column corpus baseline have no automated test coverage
payload.body:
The spec's own §4 Test Specification table lists test_sync_writes_slice_and_report, test_sync_changed_only_rewrites_drift, test_sync_preserves_memory_annotations, and test_neighbors_join_paths_with_column_pair for module M2 — none of these exist anywhere in the diff (grep across packages/ai-parrot/tests/knowledge/wiki/schema/ for "preserves_memory_annotations", "about", "wiki_remember" returns nothing under that directory; test_service.py has only 2 tests total: test_sync_then_unchanged_and_lookup and test_read_only_service_refuses_put). AC7 explicitly requires "wiki_remember(fact, link_page_id='table:…', rel='about') followed by schema sync keeps the note and it appears in the next wiki_schema_lookup" — this is untested. Manual trace of store.py's replace_schema_slice/_replace_source_slice_conn suggests the preserved-edge logic (re-adds edges whose src is external and whose dst survives in the new page set) SHOULD make this work when the table is not dropped, but this is unverified by any automated test, and the dropped-table case ("dangling edge, not a deleted note" per spec) is not exercised at all.

Separately, AC4 states ingest-ddl over "the 32 in-repo .sql files" must recover ">= 20 CREATE TABLEs and >= 329 columns" — this specific full-repo-corpus assertion (F025 baseline) has no dedicated test; test_fold_ddl_task_memory_corpus only covers the single 001_task_memory.sql file (6 tables/70 columns), and test_cli_schema.py exercises ingest-ddl only against synthetic tmp_path fixtures, never the real in-repo corpus. This numeric acceptance bar is currently unverified by CI.

Suggested fix: add test_sync_preserves_memory_annotations (per spec) exercising wiki_remember's about-edge across a sync, and add an integration test that runs ingest_ddl over the real repo's *.sql corpus (excluding .venv) and asserts the documented table/column counts.

payload.reason: Not reproducible — verified FALSE by direct source read and live test run during FEAT-600 code review. The claim was that toolkit_for() in producers/live.py unconditionally passes database_type=cfg.dialect, colliding with PostgresToolkit/BigQueryToolkit's own internal database_type kwarg. Actual code (producers/live.py:34-49) builds a kwargs dict and only adds database_type for the generic SQLToolkit fallback branch, with an explicit comment addressing exactly this collision risk. git log shows this file was touched by exactly one commit (de37b3f1b, TASK-3683) — never patched for this bug. Two independent Claude subagent reviewers converged on this identical false claim in the same review session — treated as hallucination, not a real defect.

payload.title: post-commit hook's schema ingest-ddl --changed diffs a stale ORIG_HEAD, missing DDL from plain commits
payload.body: git_hook_block() (claude_code/assets.py) is shared by the post-commit AND post-merge hooks, so `schema ingest-ddl --changed --quiet` also runs after every plain commit. _changed_ddl_paths() (cli.py) finds changed DDL with `git diff --name-only ORIG_HEAD HEAD`. ORIG_HEAD is only set by merge/reset/rebase/pull, so after a plain commit it points at whatever the last such operation left: (1) a DDL file changed by a plain commit is missed, unless it happens to fall inside the stale ORIG_HEAD..HEAD range; (2) DDL files from an old merge are re-ingested on every commit (probably harmless given changed_only, but wasted work); (3) in a checkout with no ORIG_HEAD yet, git diff fails, the command raises ClickException, and the hook's `|| true` hides it. Found while fixing issue:f5e3ca89e393 (FEAT-600, commit 7ec29c916). Suggested fix: let the hook say which range to diff, e.g. HEAD~1..HEAD (or skip ingest) in post-commit and ORIG_HEAD..HEAD in post-merge, via a per-hook block or a --since/--range option on ingest-ddl. Add a test for the post-commit case.

hooba: BBVA import E2E test has zero assertions despite its docstring claiming full coverage
payload.body: test_bbva_import_end_to_end (packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/hooba/test_integration_e2e.py:84-99) docstring claims "dry run → 0 POSTs; apply → one purchase draft per planned row; reconciled; re-run → 0 new POSTs" but the test body computes `result` from the dry-run call and never asserts on it (only comments: "May fail due to fake server limitations - that's OK for this test"). No apply/re-run phase is exercised at all. This leaves AC-11 (hooba_import_bbva_statement's dry-run/apply/resume/reconcile contract) without real end-to-end test coverage despite the suite reporting green. Suggested fix: assert result["status"]=="success", that state.purchase_invoices count is unchanged after dry_run=True, then run dry_run=False and assert one purchase-invoice draft per planned row, reconcile()["reconciled"] is True, then re-run and assert zero new POSTs (per the docstring's own stated contract).

payload.title: hooba: AC-17 no-real-data scan filter discards every match found inside tests/hooba itself
payload.body: test_no_real_data_committed (packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/hooba/test_integration_e2e.py:111-146) git-greps both packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba and packages/ai-parrot-tools/tests/hooba for forbidden patterns (real HOOBA_PASSWORD, Spanish IBAN, real session id), then filters matches with `if "test" not in line.lower() and "fixture" not in line.lower()`. Since every git-grep hit from the tests/hooba path naturally contains "test" in its own file path (e.g. "tests/hooba/..."), this filter discards 100% of matches originating from the tests directory -- the exact directory the scan is supposed to police for accidentally-committed real credentials/PII (per AC-17). A real leaked credential inside a test fixture would never be caught by this check. Suggested fix: filter on the matched line's content only (not the git-grep-prefixed file path), or scope the "test"/"fixture" exclusion to known synthetic-fixture markers rather than the substring "test" which is unavoidably present in every tests/hooba path.

payload.title: hooba: auto_open's login gate makes hooba_recover_web_session unreachable exactly when API auth is broken
payload.body: HoobaToolkit.auto_open = True (toolkit.py:73), and AbstractToolkit's ToolkitTool._execute path runs `await toolkit._ensure_open()` (which calls HoobaToolkit._open() -> self._api._ensure_session(), i.e. the API login_hook) BEFORE any tool's own body runs (parrot/tools/toolkit.py:166-169), including hooba_recover_web_session's own body. hooba_recover_web_session's entire purpose (per its docstring: "Recover a browser session and inject its sid cookie into the API jar") is to recover from a broken/expired API-cookie session via the Playwright browser fallback. But because _ensure_open() raises before the tool body runs when the API login itself is failing, the one tool designed to recover from that exact failure can never be invoked to do its job -- the auto_open gate blocks it upstream. Suggested fix: add "hooba_recover_web_session" to HoobaToolkit.exclude_tools' sibling mechanism or otherwise exempt it from the auto_open gate (e.g. a toolkit-level override, or catching the open failure specifically for this one recovery tool), so it can still run when the API session is broken.

payload.title: hooba: (name, price) line-dedup signature can silently drop legitimate duplicate lines
payload.body: _line_signature (packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/toolkit.py:463-466) builds a (name, price) tuple used by _sync_lines_and_finalize to decide whether a line already exists on a reused draft (skip re-posting it). Two genuinely distinct line items that happen to share the same name and price (a realistic case: two identical-priced products, e.g. "Consulting hour" x2 at different times, or two identical expense lines on a BBVA-derived purchase invoice) collapse to the same signature -- the second legitimate line is silently treated as "already present" and never posted, permanently losing it from the draft on any resume/retry. Suggested fix: include quantity (or a stable per-line ordinal/index) in the signature, or track posted-line identity via something more specific than (name, price) alone.

payload.title: hooba: BBVA row-count cross-check's ExcelLoader.load() call is not offloaded off the event loop
payload.body: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/bank/bbva.py:207-213 -- the independent row-count cross-check (S10) constructs an ExcelLoader and awaits its .load() call directly inside the async parse_bbva_statement path, without wrapping the (openpyxl-backed, disk-bound) load in asyncio.to_thread. This partially violates AC-11's "parses off the event loop" requirement and the repo's async-first convention (never block the event loop in async def). The primary BBVA parse path itself (_parse_bbva_sync) is correctly offloaded; only this secondary cross-check call is not. Suggested fix: wrap the ExcelLoader construction+load in asyncio.to_thread, matching the primary parse path's pattern.

payload.title: hooba: BBVA checkpoint manifest path is not scoped by Hooba account
payload.body: manifest_path_for(digest) (packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/hooba/bank/manifest.py:29-31) keys the per-statement checkpoint manifest ONLY by the statement's content digest: `$PARROT_STATE_DIR/business_automation/checkpoints/hooba_bbva_import/<digest>.manifest.json` -- there is no account/tenant component in the path. Two different Hooba accounts (e.g. two client deployments sharing one $PARROT_STATE_DIR, or a dev/staging split) that happen to import statements with byte-identical content would collide on the same manifest file, corrupting each other's resume/reconcile state. Low likelihood in practice (the digest already covers real banking data, unlikely to collide across genuinely different accounts) but a real architectural gap given the toolkit is explicitly multi-account-capable (accountId is resolved per HoobaSettings/credential). Suggested fix: include the resolved accountId (or credential_user_id) as a path segment/prefix alongside the digest.

payload.title: hooba: spec's own pseudo-code for reconcile() declared the buggy planned_rows-based signature
payload.body: sdd/specs/hooba-toolkit.spec.md:771 declares `def reconcile(m: ImportManifest, planned_rows: int) -> Dict[str, Any]` as the exact contract implementers must follow. TASK-3739's coder implemented it faithfully, sourcing rows_in from planned_rows (this run's newly-planned count) -- which is what caused the CRITICAL defect fixed in commit 9c4ba8f6f2 (a correctly-resumed or fully-complete re-run would falsely report reconciled=False, since manifest.completed/.skipped are cumulative across runs but planned_rows is not). The fix kept the spec's declared signature (to avoid an unreviewed API change) but sources rows_in from manifest.row_count instead, leaving planned_rows intentionally unused. Worth a spec update for FEAT-602 (or a callout in any future spec reusing this pattern) documenting that rows_in must come from a manifest/bundle-level stable total, not a per-call remainder count -- mirroring business_automation/ingest.py:reconcile()'s existing, explicitly-documented convention (bundle.row_count, never registrations_out alone) which this task's spec text apparently didn't cross-reference closely enough when drafting the pseudo-code.

Fixed: filter now operates on matched content only, excludes the scanner's own file; also found and fixed a deeper navconfig chdir bug that made the scan inspect the wrong checkout entirely. Verified with canary injection.

Fixed: _open() now swallows the API login failure (best-effort priming only); hooba_recover_web_session needs no API session and every other tool retries auth per-request independently. Regression test verified to fail without the fix.
Fixed: switched from a set to a Counter-based multiset for the line-dedup signature so two genuinely distinct lines sharing (name, price) both get posted.
Fixed: isolated the ExcelLoader cross-check call in its own thread+event-loop (asyncio.to_thread + asyncio.run wrapper) since the shared ExcelLoader itself is out of scope to modify.
Fixed: added optional account_id scoping to manifest_path_for/load_manifest/write_manifest, threaded through BbvaImporter and HoobaToolkit (backward compatible default).

payload.title: aggregate_records fails over JSON-2: formatted_read_group positional domain not mapped
payload.body: Live Odoo 19.0 (pokemon.helpdesk.staging, json2 transport): OdooToolkit.aggregate_records calls self._execute(model, 'formatted_read_group', [domain], kwargs) (toolkit.py:1058, and 'read_group' at :1073). Json2Transport._build_body has no mapping for these methods; the generic branch only maps a single positional arg when it looks like ids, so a domain list of tuples is dropped and Odoo answers 422 'missing a required argument: domain'. Seen when the LLM called odoo_aggregate_records on sh.helpdesk.ticket. Fix: map args[0] -> body['domain'] for read_group/formatted_read_group (and any other domain-first methods).

payload.title: parse_markdown_structure is not fence-aware: '# comment' lines inside code blocks become headings
payload.body: md_builder._HEADER_RE (^(#{1,6})\s+) is applied to every (stripped) line with no tracking of fenced code blocks, so a Python '# comment' inside a fenced block becomes a tree node. Verified: parse_markdown_structure('# Top\n\n\\\') yields nodes Top + 'comment line'. Observed while indexing the Odoo 19 Cookbook code companion with 'bookstore add-folder': chapter trees contained bogus sections like '],'. Workaround used: rewrite '# x' as '#: x' inside code blocks before indexing. Fix: skip lines while inside a fence (toggle on lines starting with three backticks or tildes).

rename_tree overwrite leaks old sidecar dir when embeddings/ subdir exists
payload.body: PageIndexToolkit.rename_tree (pageindex/toolkit.py) deletes the replaced backup via NodeContentStore.delete_tree, which only unlinks *.md and calls rmdir(); rmdir silently fails if an embeddings/ subdir exists. With embeddings enabled every overwrite re-index leaks the old tree's sidecar directory. Fix: remove the backup dir with shutil.rmtree in the backup-cleanup path, or make delete_tree remove embeddings/.

payload.title: Host toolkit with default None prefix passes resolver validation
payload.body: PR1550 a7438fffa resolver.py142-144 only compares tool_prefix when not None. AbstractToolkit defaults tool_prefix=None, so a concrete host toolkit omitting its prefix passes _host_rejection for a prefixed registry slug and emits unprefixed method names (reproduced tp_bad accepted, generated tool ping). payload.title: Review TASK-4066
Scheduler fire claim key unstable for interval/once triggers across workers (AC2 gap)
payload.body: RedisFireCoordinator.claim keys on run_times[-1].isoformat(). manager.py _create_trigger builds IntervalTrigger(**config) with no start_date (and DateTrigger without run_date defaults to now), so each worker anchors the schedule at its own trigger-creation time; two workers get different run_times, both win their claim, the agent runs twice. Cron/daily/weekly/monthly are deterministic and fine; interval auto_* jobs have no shared anchor. test_multiworker.py hands both managers an identical run_time so the suite never exercises this. Fix: quantise the claim key per interval bucket, or give DB-backed interval triggers a deterministic start_date (row created_at / hash anchor); add a test with independently built triggers. Until fixed, docs/scheduler/multi-worker.md should state interval schedules need a shared (redis) jobstore to dedupe.

payload.body: AgentSchedulerManager._handle_job_success (packages/ai-parrot-server/src/parrot/scheduler/manager.py) runs the user success_callback outside any try. wiki_sync_push is not chunked or size-capped (remote sync push)
payload.body: sync_push_remote (remote_cli.py) sends every memory page and edge in a single tools/call, and WikiSyncPushTool (tools.py) has no count/size cap. With the server app's client_max_size now 4 MiB a larger memory plane still gets HTTP 413, surfaced as an opaque '[remote:protocol] unparsable response'. Fix: chunk the client push (e.g. 200 pages / <1 MiB) and add a server-side cap with a clear error. Also WikiSyncPushTool writes without the writer lock, unlike wiki_ingest_batch.

payload.title: Remote sync LWW trusts client clocks, asserted_by and origin; pull is O(N) per page
payload.body: WikiSyncPushTool (tools.py) compares client-supplied updated_at strings lexicographically: a far-future clock or a different ISO format (Z vs +00:00, fractional seconds) can permanently win or lose. It also trusts the client's asserted_by/origin and does not origin-check the existing page, so a memory record can overwrite a non-memory page with the same concept_id (the local sync engine behaves the same). Suggest parsing/normalising timestamps and clamping to server now+skew. WikiSyncPullTool calls _synced_memory_pages (a get_page per memory page) on every cursor page; push since/cursor filtering down to the store.

payload.title: Remote client/config hardening: aiohttp errors, URL userinfo, proxy client lock, extra --link dropped
payload.body: (1) remote.py maps only ClientConnectorError/ClientOSError/TimeoutError; ServerDisconnectedError, ClientPayloadError, ClientResponseError escape as raw aiohttp exceptions instead of exit 2 with a [remote:...] prefix - catch aiohttp.ClientError as 'unreachable'. (2) WikiRemoteConfig.url (project.py _absolute_http_url) accepts userinfo and query strings that would be written verbatim to .mcp.json / .codex/config.toml; reject username/password/query and warn on bearer over plain http to a non-loopback host. (3) ProxyStdioMCPServer._client_ready (mcp_server.py) has no lock: concurrent first calls create two clients, and the client is never closed at shutdown. (4) remember in remote mode forwards only links[0]; extra --link values are silently dropped (cli.py). (5) serve.py StaticBearerKeyStore is defined inside build_key_store() rather than as the spec's module-level class, and the APIKeyRecord carries the raw token. (6) build_wiki_tools via _run_sync now initialises the Arango store in a throwaway loop for stdio; add a stdio+Arango regression test.

Postgres judge cache / baseline store reconnect and re-run DDL on every call
payload.body: PostgresJudgeCache (judge/cache.py get/set) and PostgresBaselineStore (regression.py get_baseline/record) open a new asyncpg connection and execute the full _SCHEMA_DDL on every call. payload.title: Ledger export (export_snapshot) overwrites sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl from local view instead of merging by issue_id
payload.body:
LedgerService.export_snapshot (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/service.py:424) rebuilds sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl entirely from this session's local issues (self._all_issues(), itself a replay of this checkout's events.jsonl via _sync_best_effort) and writes it unconditionally through _write_snapshot_if_changed — there is no merge against the file already on disk, and no diff against the previously-committed snapshot other than byte-equality.

/sdd-done step 9.1 (.claude/commands/sdd-done.md:412-455) calls this export from a throwaway worktree and commits whatever comes out, then restores the main worktree's staged/working copy to match.

Failure mode: if a worktree's local ledger log is behind origin (e.g. built from an older origin/<base> before another concurrent session pushed new `ledger open`/`close` events — a known hazard per [[worktree-concurrent-sdd-worker]] and [[shared-checkout-branching-hazard]]), export_snapshot only knows about issues it has replayed locally. Running /sdd-done in that worktree regenerates issues.jsonl from an incomplete view and silently drops rows for issues opened/closed by the other session, overwriting the shared committed snapshot with a regression.

Suggested fix: export_snapshot should merge by issue_id against the existing committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl (union, keep rows present on disk that are absent from the local replay, let only genuinely superseded/compacted issue_ids be dropped) rather than treating the local view as authoritative — or /sdd-done should refuse the export (abort step 9.1) if the local ledger log's cursor lags origin for issues.jsonl's branch, rather than committing a shrinking diff unattended.

payload.title: Ledger export (export_snapshot) overwrites sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl instead of reconciling against the committed snapshot
payload.body:
Supersedes issue:1e13dd5b188b (closed: that issue's suggested fix — a flat row-level merge by issue_id — was insufficient and is replaced by this reconciliation design).

LedgerService.export_snapshot (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/ledger/service.py:424) rebuilds sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl entirely from this session's local issues (self._all_issues(), a replay of this checkout's local events.jsonl via _sync_best_effort) and writes it unconditionally through _write_snapshot_if_changed, with no reconciliation against the file already committed on disk.

/sdd-done step 9.1 (.claude/commands/sdd-done.md:412-455) calls this export from a throwaway worktree and commits whatever comes out.

Failure mode: if this checkout's local ledger event log never recorded issues opened/closed by another session/machine (events.jsonl is local, not itself git-synced — only the periodic issues.jsonl snapshot is committed), export_snapshot has no way to know about them and silently drops their rows from the shared committed snapshot. See [[worktree-concurrent-sdd-worker]] / [[shared-checkout-branching-hazard]] for the same class of concurrent-session hazard.

A flat JSON-row merge by issue_id against the committed file is NOT the right fix: issues.jsonl is a derived STATE snapshot, not raw events, so for any issue_id present in both local and committed versions there is no principled way to pick a winner from the snapshot alone (could produce duplicate issue_ids or resurrect an already-closed issue).

Correct fix — reconcile at export time, two-tier:
1. For issue_ids the local ledger log HAS seen (has at least one event for), the local derived state is authoritative (it legitimately includes any close/claim this session applied) — use it as-is.
2. For issue_ids present in the currently-committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl but absent from the local event log entirely, there is no local event to replay — carry those rows forward UNCHANGED into the new snapshot (do not drop them just because this session never saw them).
3. Only an issue_id with a local close/compaction event should actually disappear from the output.

Implementation sketch: before building new_content, read+parse the existing dest file (or the committed blob at HEAD if dest is mid-overwrite in a throwaway worktree), collect issue_ids with zero local events, and union their raw rows into `rows` prior to the sort — rather than attempting any kind of cross-machine event-log sync (there is no shared event transport to sync from).

payload.reason: Superseded by issue:62038221413a — the flat row-level JSON merge-by-issue_id this issue suggested is insufficient (issues.jsonl is a derived state snapshot, not raw events, so a naive merge could resurrect closed issues or produce conflicting duplicates). Replaced by a two-tier reconciliation design: local-authoritative for issue_ids the local event log has seen, carry-forward-unchanged for issue_ids known only to the committed snapshot.

export_snapshot now reconciles against the committed sdd/ledger/issues.jsonl: rows for issue_ids the local ledger has never recorded are carried forward unchanged, local state stays authoritative for known ids, locally compacted issues still drop; `wikitoolkit ledger export --no-reconcile` is the explicit destructive opt-out and /sdd-done §9.1 documents the invariant. Verified on the real ledger: 279 committed rows → 286 exported, 0 dropped (FEAT-671, TASK-4295/4296/4297, branch feat-FEAT-671-commands-sdd-done-fixes).

payload.title: Extract a programmatic build_wiki() from the wikitoolkit build click callback
payload.body:
The repository-scan build pipeline has no programmatic entry point: its logic lives inside the click callback `build` (packages/ai-parrot/src/parrot/knowledge/wiki/cli.py:1560) and its nested `_pipeline()`. Every non-CLI caller must therefore shell out to the `wikitoolkit` console script (`parrot.knowledge.wiki.entry:main`, packages/ai-parrot/pyproject.toml:204).

Context: raised as brainstorm Option C and spec §8 Q2 of FEAT-672 (github-reviewer-local-repo-wiki), which needs to build a graph over a cloned repository from inside a long-lived aiohttp agent. FEAT-672 deliberately did NOT do this: the narrow `wikitoolkit build --storage-dir` flag it adds removes the blocking motivation, and extracting the pipeline is a wikitoolkit-core refactor with a far larger blast radius (vault mode, Roblox enrichment, language fingerprints, OKF export, graph.html, remote push all hang off that callback).

Remaining motivation, recorded so it is not lost: (1) the build cannot be tested end-to-end without spawning a process; (2) callers are coupled to the `wikitoolkit` script being resolvable on the host process's PATH/venv — a missing binary silently disables the feature; (3) error handling is exit-code granularity, and stdout is unusable as data because the navconfig banner precedes any output.

Suggested fix when a second in-process caller appears: lift `_pipeline()` into `build_wiki(root, config, *, force, no_export, no_graph, storage_dir, ...) -> BuildReport`, keep `wiki_write_lock` (project.py:76) inside it, and reduce the click callback to argument parsing plus a call. Do not do this speculatively — FEAT-672 is the only consumer today and it is served by the flag.

payload.title: executor _action_click text-contains path passes args to execute_script — breaks under Playwright/Page drivers
payload.body:
Where: packages/ai-parrot-tools/src/parrot_tools/scraping/executor.py, _action_click (~line 449-516), the js_text_filter branch (click selector with `:-soup-contains(...)`).

What: it calls `await driver.execute_script(script, selector, js_text_filter)` with a script that reads `arguments[0]` / `arguments[1]`. PlaywrightDriver.execute_script (drivers/playwright_driver.py:265) and PageDriver.execute_script (drivers/page_driver.py:173) map to `self._page.evaluate(script, *args)`. Playwright's `page.evaluate(expression, arg=None)` accepts a single optional arg and has no `arguments` object, so the call raises TypeError (two positional args) / ReferenceError, and the click step fails. Only SeleniumDriver (execute_script with *args) works.

Why it matters: any catalogued browsing/scraping action that clicks by text-contains fails on the default Playwright/Obscura path used by WebBrowsingToolkit.

Suggested fix: build an IIFE expression with the selector and needle embedded via json.dumps and call `driver.evaluate(expr)` (portable: Playwright evaluates the expression; Selenium evaluate prepends `return`). Same pattern FEAT-681 adopts for the `submit` action. Add a test asserting execute_script is not called with extra args. Out of scope of FEAT-681 (sdd/specs/browsing-executor-action-gaps.spec.md §1 Non-Goals).

payload.reason: _action_click text-contains path now runs a json.dumps-embedded IIFE via driver.evaluate instead of execute_script(script, *args) with arguments[N]; driver-neutral across Selenium/Playwright/Page. Tests added.

payload.title: executor _action_scroll bottom height_script starts with 'return' — SyntaxError under Playwright/Page drivers
payload.body: _action_scroll(direction='bottom') calls driver.execute_script('return Math.max(document.body.scrollHeight, ...)'). Selenium wraps scripts in a function body so 'return' is legal; PlaywrightDriver/PageDriver forward to page.evaluate(script), where a top-level 'return' is an 'Illegal return statement' SyntaxError, so scroll-to-bottom (lazy-load trigger) fails on those drivers. Fix: use driver.evaluate('Math.max(...)') (Selenium's evaluate prefixes return). Found while fixing issue:c10c1e94f4b3 (FEAT-682).
